Let’s be the Actors of tomorrow’s world!!

The Airshed situated inside B2 Rockview Apartments Vasant Kunj, offers you a chance to reconnect with nature.
New Delhi, the capital of India, is one of the most polluted cities in the world. Therefore, Swechha is looking to revive a community park and transform it into a place where native species can regain their space. This park is unique and acts as an exemplar for us and our future generations. Thanks to the investment of Swechha and its numerous volunteers, the Airshed acts as the lungs of the surrounding neighbourhood.

Every Tuesday, volunteers from WWF join us and you can do too!
Come, join us and make a positive impact! Amazing projects such as designing of a butterfly garden, an air detox garden and a herb garden are waiting to be built by you! All volunteers are welcome!

Why participate?

It’s a great opportunity to learn practical skills, increase your knowledge about nature, meet like- minded individuals, share good vibes and be thankful to Mother Earth.

Session : Every Tuesday from 8 to 12am !

Event Lead:
Anna Zimmer- anna@swehha.in

Swechha’s Airshed park in Vasant Kunj is home to around 400+ trees – and with them, to hundreds of birds that chirp in the middle of the greenery every morning. Volunteers and members from the community joined us for a special birdwatching session during the Great Backyard Bird Count (GBBC) 2018. GBBC is a global event taking place in February to understand the population development and movement of our winged companions. Since 2013, India is an active participant to this event, and thousands of birdwatchers have contributed to listing the species found all over the country.

This year, Swechha India was part of the GBBC, too, and participants got to enjoy the serene beauty of the park on a winter morning, listen to the sounds of nature, observe and learn to identify birds under the guidance of an experienced birder.

When: 17th Feb, 8am-10am

Where: B2, Vasant Kunj,

title.rendered: Yamuna Shramdaan 2017 with Ivolunteer and Synopsis

content.rendered:
In the wake of the festive season and all the widespread litter and dumping of idols in the river Yamuna, a group of 65 volunteers from iVolunteer-Your Skills can change lives, Synopsis and Swechha, decided to make the most of their Saturday morning by cleaning up all the mess and litter that had been left behind on the banks of the river at Kudsia Ghat near Kashmere Gate.

We thank the team at Ivolunteer and Synopsis, for joining us in making this Shramdaan a success!

Gram Anubhav is a unique educational trip which takes high school students on a journey of exploration, reflection and action into rural India. It is an opportunity to experience and realize the other India. It allows students to explore the physical, social, economic and cultural aspects of an Indian village while integrating what they have learnt from textbooks and in classrooms. The rural exposure camp is packed with energisers, interesting activities, brainstorming sessions, interactions with the local communities, village visits and Shramdaan.
This year, over 150 high school students from Delhi traveled with us to Bodh Gaon, the rural campus of Bodh Shiksha Samiti in a tiny hamlet surrounded by the Aravali hills, not too far from the Sariska Tiger Reserve.

Delhi is one of the most polluted cities in the world. We want to change this by planting thousands of trees this monsoon, with your help.

We have been actively involved in multiple plantation drives since 2005, having planted over 30,000 trees around Delhi NCR, with an average rate of survival of 80%. Monsoon Wooding is one such action-packed annual Swechha campaign that aims at conserving and creating green spaces. In 2013, we created Delhi’s first urban mini forest at St Mary’s School, Dwarka and there has been no looking back since. We planted Faridabad’s first Urban forest in 2014, once almost a barren land, now a lush green landscape.  This was followed by creation of Gurgaon’s first food forest and butterfly garden in 2015 with over 1500 saplings.

In 2016, over 2500 saplings were adopted by individuals on Bitgiving that led to the creation of forests, herb gardens and butterfly gardens in Delhi and Gurgaon. In total, over 10,000 saplings including herbs and shrubs were planted over the last one year.

This year, we aim to bring the jungles back to the city by planting thousands of saplings. Help us reclaim the green cover by volunteering with us for the drives. Write to us at volunteer@swechha.in or call at 011 29544678 to get more details.

Pagdandi Summer School 2017

45 kids aged 8-16 , 12 activities, 20 days!

The Pagdandi Summer School is a learning programme conducted by Swechha during the summer vacations for the children and adolescents of Jagdamba Camp. The School aims to become a space for the children to be purposefully engaged in learning skills and values for their growth as individuals and young leaders.

Summer School 2017 started on June 1st and will ended on June 24th with a showcase! This year, the kids spent their summer learning Dance, Theatre, Art and Craft, Storytelling, Crochet, and a whole lot more!  The programme is supported by KHD.

The school ended with an energetic and emotionally driven showcase on the 24th of June, where each child participated and showcased their individual journey through the school.
